title: Creatures
build: Thalamus's two-sided disk release, G64 images of side A (SHA-256 4544cf5d…) and side B (b30bb735…) from the C64 Preservation Project's collection; the title says 1990, the collection 1991 (orientation.md)

records.c: The 6510's port, choosing the memory map: intro_start writes $36 (BASIC ROM out), title_clear and title_2_start $35 (I/O, no ROMs), so the interrupt vectors come from RAM at $FFFA-$FFFF.
Not a variable of the title's: title_2_clear's STA at $9906 writes $D8 here, which looks meant for $D016 (see $98EB). Nothing in the title reads it.
The byte nothing reads: the BIT $00A9 at $05EC is there only to hide the LDA #$00 in its operand (at $05ED, a branch target) from the path that runs into it.
colour_bars' mask, 7: it ANDs each line's number with it to pick out every eighth line.
Read only for time: the BIT $EA at $95D5 in title_raster_1 spends three cycles to place the colour bars on the line.
Low byte of the music data pointer of the voice being played ($FC/$FD), saved per voice in music_ptr_lo/hi.
High byte of the music data pointer.
The SID register offset of the voice being played (0, 7 or 14).
The player's work byte (the note length's high part in music_next_note, the loop count in music_cmd_loop and the section offset's high byte in music_cmd_call).

Music-on flag: music_frame runs the player only while it is set; music_init sets it and music_stop clears it. The player from here to $0B33 is the engine's (music_on is at $0334 there) assembled $CC bytes higher: the same bytes apart from the addresses. intro_start moves it here from $2300-$2AFF in the file.

Music player, one tick per frame for the three voices. A speed counter ($0964 against $0963) decides on which frames the voices read new commands; a global filter sweep adds $0980/$0981 to the shadow cutoff $0A26/$0A27 every frame. For each voice (X = 2 down to 0, SID register offset from $0A07) it reads two-byte commands at the voice's data pointer ($0A04/$0A01): a first byte below $25 picks a command from the jump table at $0A2A/$0A4F (the JSR at $0499 is rewritten to point at it), with the second byte in A; otherwise the voice's note timer, effects (portamento $0831, vibrato $076C, waveform choice, arpeggio $073D, pulse sweep $06E7) and gate are updated in the shadow registers at $0A11.
The global filter sweep: music_filter_step_lo added to the cutoff's low three bits (wrapping past 7 with a carry) and music_filter_step_hi to its high byte.

The voice loop, X = 2 down to 0. Y and $FE get the voice's register offset; music_step_count counts the frames to the next step (music_step_rate), when music_step and the three-step music_cycle3 move on; the voice's data pointer goes to $FC/$FD.
On the frame music_tick wraps to 0, music_note_age counts up, and the voice reads commands if its note is about to end: a length high byte of $FF (no note yet), or 0 with a low byte of 1.

Reads a command: a first byte of $01-$25 (less 1, an index into music_cmd_lo/hi) puts its handler's address in the JSR at $0499, which runs it with the second byte in A and the register offset in Y; then music_advance and the next command. Any other byte ends the voice's commands for this frame.
Operand of the JSR at $0499: the address of the music command handler, written from the jump tables each time a command is read.

High byte of the handler address in the JSR at $0499 (the low byte is $049A), both written from music_cmd_lo and music_cmd_hi. After the handler the loop reads the next item (music_advance). Once a note is reached, the voice's frame work runs from $04A1: portamento once the note is older than music_porta_delay, vibrato when it has a depth, and the attack waveform: values 1 to 5 put waveform music_waveforms_m1[value] in the voice's control register for the first music_attack_len frames of the note; values 6 and up alternate waveform value - 5 with the note's own control byte (music_ctrl) on every other step.

In music_update, where attack values 6 and up subtract 5 to pick their waveform; from $04DC the 1-5 case tests the note's age against music_attack_len, the chosen control byte goes to the voice's shadow register at $0A15, then the arpeggio and pulse sweep run when set, the note timer counts down on the music's tick, the voice's data pointer ($FC/$FD) is saved to music_ptr_lo/hi, and the loop moves to the next voice.
On the tempo frame, music_note_timer; then the voice's data pointer is saved and the loop moves on to the next voice.

Operand of the CPX at $0521: where music_update's voice loop stops (after the DEX, the loop ends once X minus this is negative). 0 plays all three voices. The file holds $FF here; intro_start writes the 0.
Counts down the current note's length ($09FE/$09B3, a 16-bit count per voice); near the end it clears the gate bit in the voice's shadow control register, and at zero it falls into music_next_note.

Starts the next note of a voice: clears the voice's effect counters, reloads ADSR and pulse width from the voice's instrument settings ($09D7, $09CE, $09D4), reads the note byte (zero is a rest), converts it with music_note_freq (adding the transpose and an optional second interval for arpeggio), stores the frequency in the shadow registers and the voice's state, then reads the length byte. A note byte of $19 takes a further length byte.
When this is the filter voice (music_filter_voice), the filter restarts: cutoff low bits 0, high byte from music_filter_start.
The note's attack/decay, sustain/release and pulse width from the voice's settings, and the vibrato's wait reloaded.

The note byte, kept in music_note: 0 is a rest. Otherwise the arpeggio's second note (music_arp_interval semitones up) and a glide target (music_glide_interval) are worked out, then the note's own frequency.
Stores the frequency in the shadow registers and music_freq_lo/hi, the length byte in music_len_lo, and starts the note with the voice's control byte (music_wave).

A next command of $19 gives a long note: its second byte becomes the length's high byte (music_len_hi). Command 25's own handler is a bare RTS ($07BD), so the command loop passes over it. Otherwise the BIT at $05EC hides the LDA #$00 at $05ED and the high byte is 0.

Starts the tune whose header $FC/$FD points at. Clears the player's 155 bytes of state ($0962-$09FC), gives each voice a release point of 2, a note length of 1 and a vibrato period of 1, and sets the tempo $0963 to 1. Keeps the header address in $0A0A/$0A0B as the base for section calls. Voice 1's data starts right after the four-byte header; the header holds two 16-bit offsets, relative to that point, for voices 2 and 3. Then silences the shadow registers, runs two ticks and sets the music-on flag $0400.
Each voice gets release point 2, note length 1 (high byte 0) and vibrato period 1; the tempo is 1.

The header: its address is kept as music_tune_base and voice 1's pointer is the header + 4. The loop at $0630 (X from $7E, so its stores land on voices 2 and 3 of music_ptr_lo/hi) adds each 16-bit offset to voice 1's pointer.
Silences the shadow registers, runs two ticks (music_tick_and_copy) and sets music_on.
Clears the music-on flag $0400, then (entered at $065A) clears the 24 shadow SID registers $0A11-$0A28 and the volume register $D418. music_cmd_end calls it; music_init enters at $065A.
Clears the shadow SID registers $0A11-$0A28 and the SID's volume and filter register.
Music command: repeat a section. Counts the voice's loop counter ($09DD,X) up; until it reaches the count in A, jumps the data pointer back to the address saved by music_cmd_loop_mark.

Music command: mark the start of a repeated section, saving the voice's data pointer in $09E3/$09E9 and clearing its loop counter. $0696 and $069E are the same pair of commands for a second, nested loop level (offset by three voices).

Music command 18: music_cmd_loop for the second, nested loop level, the same with Y three voices on ($09E0 for the count, $09E6/$09EC for the saved pointer). Command 19, at $069E, is music_cmd_loop_mark's twin for that level.

Music commands that each store A into one voice setting: $06A4 transpose ($09C5), $06A8 note release point ($097A, or $0971 above 99), $06B6 waveform choice ($0977, or the voice whose notes drive the filter, $0962, above 98), $06C4 pulse sweep limits ($09BF high nibble, $09C2 low nibble), $06D3 vibrato period ($09FB), $06D7 filter resonance and routing ($0A28), $06DB filter start ($0982), $06DF adds A to the volume and filter mode ($0A29).
Sweeps a voice's pulse width (shadow $0A13/$0A14) up and down by the step in $09DA between the limits held in $09BF and $09C2, turning at each.
Music command: sets the voice's control (waveform and gate) byte $09D1.
Arpeggio, mode 1: on alternate frames ($09AD bit 0) puts the note's second frequency ($0986/$0989) or its own frequency into the shadow registers.
Vibrato: after a delay ($0995), moves the frequency up or down by the depth $0992 each frame through music_freq_up/down, changing direction every $09FB frames in a four-step cycle ($09B9).

Music commands that store A into a setting: $07A4 arpeggio interval ($09A1), $07A8 filter sweep step (high five bits to $0981, low three to $0980), $07B6 tempo ($0963), $07BA second-note interval ($099E), $07BE adds A to the transpose ($09C5), $07C6 vibrato delay ($0998).
Music command 33: sets the voice's vibrato delay ($0998), reached through music_cmd_lo/hi like the other commands.
Music command: return from a called section, restoring the data pointer saved by music_cmd_call ($09EF/$09F5) and the outer saved one.
Music command: fine tune added to every note's frequency ($09B0).
Adds the vibrato depth $0992 to the voice's 16-bit frequency ($0965/$0968) and writes it to the shadow registers; $07FC subtracts it.
Subtracts the vibrato depth from the voice's frequency and writes it to the shadow registers (the other half of music_freq_up).
Converts a note number (bits 0-6, plus the voice's transpose $09C5) to a SID frequency from the table at $0A74, adds the fine tune $09B0, and returns it in A (low) and Y (high).
Music command: high byte of the portamento step ($09CB); $095A sets the low byte ($09C8).
Portamento: mode 1 glides the frequency towards the target note ($0986/$0989) from either side and stops on it, mode 3 glides down, mode 2 glides up. Steps are $09C8/$09CB.

Mode 1: compares the frequency with the target (music_porta_hi/lo) and steps towards it, up through $088D or down through $08A0; once it reaches or passes the target, the frequency is set to the target.
Steps the frequency up by music_porta_step_lo/hi, and writes it to the voice's shadow registers and music_freq_lo/hi.
Steps the frequency down by the portamento step, the other half of $088D.
Music command: pulse-width sweep step ($09DA).
Moves the voice's data pointer $FC/$FD on by one two-byte command.
Starts a tune: Y and X are the low and high bytes of its header. Turns the player off while music_init sets it up.

Music commands that store A into one voice setting: $08DC portamento delay ($098C), $08E0 vibrato depth ($0992), $08E4 portamento mode ($0983), $08E8 arpeggio mode ($0974), $08EC step rate ($097D), $08F0 attack/decay ($09D7), $08F4 volume and filter mode ($0A29), $0933 sustain/release ($09CE), $095E pulse width high byte ($09D4).
Music command 6: sets the voice's step rate for the arpeggio and three-step cycle ($097D), reached through music_cmd_lo/hi.
Music command: sets the attack and decay of the voice's notes ($09D7), reached through the command tables; $08F4 is the next one, which sets the volume (music_volume).
Music command: converts A to a frequency and makes it the portamento target ($0989/$0986).

Music command: call a section. Saves the return pointer (two levels, $09EF/$09F5 and $09F2/$09F8), then jumps the voice's data pointer to the tune base plus the 16-bit offset given by A and the next byte.
Music command: end of tune. Stops the music and drops the player's two return addresses, so the frame's update ends there.

Called once a frame by the title's main loop (the JSR at $94E3, after the raster routine sets title_frame): when the music-on flag $0400 is set, runs music_update and copies the 25 shadow registers $0A11-$0A29 to the SID at $D400-$D418.
Runs music_update and copies the shadow registers to the SID, without checking the music-on flag (music_init calls it twice).
Operand of the LDY at $0947: the first shadow register music_frame copies to the SID ($18, counting down).

Operand of the CPY at $0952: the shadow register below which copying stops. 0 copies down to $D400, all voices. The file holds $FF, which would stop after the first register written, $D418; intro_start writes the 0.
RTS of the last command handler. music_init addresses $0961,Y with Y from 155 down to 1, so this is the base of the state it clears ($0962-$09FC), not a target of its own.
The voice (0-2) whose every new note restarts the filter sweep: the cutoff is reset from $0982 when that voice starts a note. Set by a music command ($06B6, values above 98).
Tempo: the number of frames between the frames on which the voices read new commands.
Frame counter for the tempo; the voices read commands on the frame it wraps to zero.
Current frequency of each voice, low byte (three bytes, one per voice; the high bytes are at $0968).
Current frequency of each voice, high byte.
The note each voice is playing (zero for a rest).
Each voice's control byte (waveform and gate) for the current note, copied from $09D1 when the note starts.
Release point of each voice: when the note's remaining length (low byte, high byte zero) falls below it, the gate bit is cleared.
Arpeggio mode of each voice (0 off); see music_arpeggio.

Attack waveform of each voice: 0 none, 1-5 a control byte from music_waveforms used for the first frames of each note ($097A frames), then the note's own control byte. Values of 6 and more take the path at $04CC.
Number of frames the attack waveform lasts at the start of each note (0: the whole note).
Frames per step of the arpeggio and the three-step cycle of each voice.
Filter sweep: added to the cutoff's low three bits each frame (set with $0981 by music command $07A8).
Filter sweep: added to the cutoff's high byte each frame, with the carry from $0980.
Filter cutoff (high byte) that the sweep restarts from on each note of the filter voice.

Portamento mode of each voice: 0 off, 1 glide to the target note, 2 up, 3 down (three bytes; $0984 and $0985 are the second and third voice's, also written by music_init's header loop through $0984,X).
The second and third voices' portamento modes (see music_porta_mode), which music_init's header loop also writes.
Portamento target frequency of each voice, low byte; music_init's header loop also stores through $0987,X (X from $7E) into the voice pointers.
The second and third voices' portamento targets, low bytes (see music_porta_lo), also written by music_init's header loop.
Portamento target frequency of each voice, high byte.
Frames after the start of a note before the portamento starts.
Frames since the voice's current note started (cleared at each note, counted each tick); compared with the portamento delay and the attack length.
Vibrato depth of each voice: the frequency step per frame (0 off).
Vibrato delay counter of each voice, reloaded from $0998 at each note.
Vibrato delay of each voice, in frames.
A counter of each voice stepping 0, 1, 2 every $097D frames, cleared at each note.
Glide interval of each voice: when not zero, each note glides towards the note this many semitones away (music_cmd_porta_target).
Arpeggio interval of each voice, the semitones of the second note (read at $059C).
The three voices' arpeggio notes, the frequency's low byte that music_arpeggio writes on the arpeggio's second step.
The three voices' arpeggio notes, high byte, set by music_next_note and written by music_arpeggio.
Frame counter of each voice towards the next arpeggio step ($097D).
Arpeggio step counter of each voice; bit 0 picks which of the two frequencies plays.
Fine tune of each voice, added to every note's frequency.
Remaining length of the voice's note, high byte ($FF before the first note); the low byte is at $09FE.
Vibrato frame counter of each voice, towards a change of direction every $09FB frames.
Vibrato phase of each voice, a four-step cycle (up, down, down, up).
Pulse sweep direction of each voice.
Pulse sweep upper limit of each voice.
Pulse sweep lower limit of each voice.
Transpose of each voice, in semitones.
Portamento step of each voice, low byte.
Portamento step of each voice, high byte.
Sustain and release of each voice's notes.
Control byte (waveform) of each voice's notes, copied into the note at its start.
Pulse width (high byte) of each voice's notes.
Attack and decay of each voice's notes.
Pulse sweep step of each voice (0 off).
Repeat counters of each voice, two levels ($09DD and $09E0).
Saved data pointer (low bytes) of each voice's repeated sections, two levels.
Saved data pointer (high bytes) of each voice's repeated sections, two levels.
Return pointers (low bytes) of each voice's called sections, two levels.
Second-level return pointers (low bytes) of each voice's called sections.
Return pointers (high bytes) of each voice's called sections.
Second-level return pointers (high bytes) of each voice's called sections.
Vibrato period of each voice: frames between changes of direction.
Remaining length of the voice's note, low byte (high byte $09B3).
Data pointer of each voice, high byte.
Data pointer of each voice, low byte.
SID register offsets of the three voices: 0, 7 and 14.
Address of the tune's header (low $0A0A, high $0A0B), the base for section calls.
High byte of the tune base; also the base of the waveform table, which music_update indexes as $0A0B,Y with Y from 1 to 5 (the table proper starts at $0A0C).
Control bytes chosen by a voice's waveform setting 1-5: pulse ($41), sawtooth ($21), triangle ($11), noise ($81), pulse and triangle ($51).
Shadow copy of the SID registers $D400-$D418, written by the player and copied out by music_frame each frame.
Shadow of voice 1's frequency high byte; with Y = 0, 7 or 14, the same register of each voice ($D401, $D408, $D40F).
Shadow of the voice's pulse width, low byte (indexed by the voice's register offset).
Shadow of the voice's pulse width, high byte.
Shadow of the voice's control register (waveform and gate).
Shadow of the voice's attack and decay.
Shadow of the voice's sustain and release; $0A1E and $0A25 are the second and third voices' (the shadow continues to $0A29).
Shadow of the filter cutoff, low three bits ($D415).
Shadow of the filter cutoff, high byte ($D416).
Shadow of the filter resonance and voice routing ($D417).
Shadow of the filter mode and volume ($D418).
Low bytes of the 37 music command handlers, indexed by the command number minus one; the high bytes follow at $0A4F.
High bytes of the 37 music command handlers (see music_cmd_lo).
SID frequencies of 96 notes, eight octaves from C-0 ($0116) to B-7 ($F810), two bytes each, low byte first.
music_freq_table read from its second byte: music_note_freq takes each frequency's high byte at $0A75,Y (low byte at $0A74,Y), Y being twice the note; these 64 bytes are the table's first 32 entries.
music_freq_table from note 32 (the high byte of its frequency, read at $0AB5,Y) to the table's end at $0B33.
185 bytes of $FF to $0BEC: the file's own filler at $2A34-$2AEC, between the player's tables and intro_start, moved here with them.

A copy of the first 19 bytes of intro_start ($2AED-$2AFF in the file: SEI, LDA #$36, STA $01, CLI, LDA #$00, STA $D015, STA $D01C, STA $D020, and STA $D021's opcode and low byte), carried here when intro_start moves $2300-$2AFF to $0400-$0BFF. Nothing runs it here; the high byte of that last store is at $2B00.
Where the move in intro_setup leaves the operand of its STA $0400,X (at $2B64) after its eight pages: one page past the copy. Nothing is stored here.

The high byte ($D0) of STA $D021, the last instruction of intro_start's first 20 bytes. The boot program starts intro_start at $2AED in the file: interrupts off and on around the memory map $36 (BASIC ROM out), then sprites off, sprite multicolour off and a black border and background. intro_setup goes on to move $2300-$2AFF to $0400-$0BFF and fill those pages with $FF, so in the running title only this byte of that start is left; the moved copy of the rest is at $0BED.

The rest of intro_start. Blanks the screen, initialises the drive (drive_init sends "I"), points the VIC at bank 1 ($DD00 bits 0-1 = 2, $4000-$7FFF) with the screen at $4400 and characters at $4800 ($D018 = $12), switches the display back on with 40 columns, and sets colour RAM $D800-$DBE8 to black. Then it copies the fast loader at $2C00-$2FFF to $C000-$C3FF and moves the music player and its tables, $2300-$2AFF, to $0400-$0BFF.
VIC bank 1: CIA 2's port A bits 0-1 made outputs and set to 2.
Colour RAM to 0, black: $D800-$DBE8 in four overlapping stretches of 251 bytes (X from $FB down to 1).
Copies the fast loader, four pages from $2C00, to $C000-$C3FF.

The move: eight pages from $2300 to $0400, each source byte replaced by $FF behind it. The loop steps the high bytes of its three operands (INC $2B63, $2B66, $2B6B) after each page, so in the running program they read $2B00 and $0C00, one page past the end.
High byte of the operand of the LDA $2300,X at $2B61, stepped a page at a time by the move (INC $2B63): it reads $2B after the eighth page.
High byte of the operand of the STA $0400,X at $2B64, stepped with it: $0C after the move.
High byte of the operand of the STA $2300,X at $2B69 that fills the source with $FF, stepped with the others: $2B after the move.

Patches the title for this load. The fire exit at $94F2 becomes JMP load_game (the file has JMP $1600), and music_play's arguments at $9913 become the tune at $3800 (the file has LDX #$00 / LDY #$9E); music_frame's call at $94E3 and music_play's at $9917 are written with the values they already hold.

Sets the player's two voice limits to 0 (music_update's loop operand at $0522 and music_frame's copy operand at $0953, both $FF in the file) so all three voices play, and music_frame's first register to $18 (as in the file); then starts the title at title_entry.

The title's fire exit, once intro_setup has patched it in: interrupts off, then 0 to the SID's volume register $D418, 25 times over (the STA in the loop has no index). Copies $2F00-$2F30 to $0190-$01C0 and jumps to the fast loader at $C000. The loader loads side A's GAME file (its name is at $2BCE) and jumps to $0190; that code maps all RAM in ($01 = $34), moves $5C00-$B7FF up to $A400-$FFFF a page at a time from the top, and jumps to $1000 to start the game.
"GAME", the four-letter name the fast loader at $C000 passes to SETNAM (from $2BCE, length 4).
Opens channel 15 of drive 8 with the one-letter command at $2BEF ("I", initialise the disk), closes it and restores the default channels (CLRCHN, which it jumps to).
"I", the drive's initialise command, sent by drive_init.
16 bytes nothing reads or runs: a zero, then STA $8B; LDX $120C; CLC; LDA $8B; ADC $2B22,X; STA $8B; RTS and a lone JSR opcode. Code left in memory when the file was saved; no other file holds it.

The title tune, played by music_play from intro_setup's patched call: a four-byte header (voice 2's and 3's offsets, $0091 and $02C2, from voice 1's start at $3804), then the three voices' commands to $3B86, and the sections they call (music_cmd_call) to $3C8B.
The title tune's second voice, to its end command at $3AC5.
The title tune's third voice, to its end command at $3B86.
The sections the three voices call (at offsets from the header, $3B87, $3C10, $3C23, $3C2E, $3C3F, $3C4A, $3C55, $3C5C and $3C75), each ending with a return; the last ends at $3C8B.

The second byte of the title tune's last return command ($24 at $3C8B): the player reads it into A and the return ignores it. It is also the first byte of the leftover code after the tune (an STA $3CA3 that nothing runs; see the exclusion from $3C8D).
The last byte of VIC bank 0, which the VIC shows in the gaps it opens when it is in that bank. title_2_start zeroes it, and $7FFF, the same byte of bank 1, which is the bank the title uses.

The Thalamus logo's characters as drawn: codes 0-$4C to $5267 (code 0 blank), multicolour, with black as the characters' own colour and the shared dark grey and grey (logo_mc1, logo_mc2). logo_dissolve copies them into the live set at $4800 a few bits at a time; it and logo_wipe work on the first 756 bytes. The rest, $5268-$53FF, is zeros.
logo_chars from byte $FA (character $1F, its row 2): the second of the three 250-byte blocks logo_dissolve works on, copied to $48FA.
logo_chars from byte $1F4 (character $3E, its row 4): the third block, copied to $49F4, which runs to $52F3 although the logo ends at $5267.
Sprite shapes $60-$6A of VIC bank 1, 64 bytes each to $5ABF: the single-colour letters A, H, T, L, U, M, S, E, N, R and P, from which thalamus_frames and presents_frames spell THALAMUS and PRESENTS.
21 more 64-byte sprite blocks ($6B-$7F) to $5FFF that nothing shows. They are zeros, with $BD as the last byte of most, except $5B00-$5CFF, which holds a message (apex_message).

A message in ASCII that nothing prints, in 32-character lines: "YO!" and "CHECK THIS OUT", "THE APEX BOYZ ARE BACK!", "WITH THE FOLLOW UP TO THE SUPERB SHOOT-EM-UP "RETROGRADE"", then APEX! in big letters drawn with $D1 characters, then rows of asterisks to $5CFF. Apex Computer Productions are credited in the scroller (scroll_text).
Sprite blocks $74-$7F, zeros with $BD in each block's last byte, to $5FFF.

The Creatures logo, a multicolour bitmap: the first six character rows of the bitmap at $6000 (320 bytes a row, to $677F), shown in bitmap mode from line $31 to $61 by title_raster_1, with its colours from logo_screen (at $4000) and logo_colour (at $D800) and a black background.
logo_bitmap from row 3, column 8, to its end at $677F; the 128 bytes after it, to $67FF, are zeros.

The scroller's character set, 256 characters to $6FFF ($D018 = $0A). Each letter is four characters: its code (top left), code + $40 (top right), code + $80 (bottom left) and code + $C0 (bottom right). The codes are the text's ASCII with bit 6 off ($01-$1A for A-Z, $20 for a space). The shapes are holes in solid blocks, so the colour bars behind the scroller show through them.
scroller_font from character $80: the bottom halves of the letters.

The credits' character set, to $77FF ($D018 = $0C), letters drawn as holes in solid blocks (the space, $20, is solid), so that colour_bars' colours show in them. Screen codes $01-$3F for the small capitals of PROGRAMMED BY, GRAPHICS & MUSIC BY, PRESS FIRE TO LOAD and the copyright; other codes, up to $F1, for the names' two-row letters.
credits_font from character $80: more of the names' two-row letters.

The credits as they sit on the screen, 768 bytes to $7AFF, copied to rows 6-24 ($40F0-$43EF) by title_2_loop when the logo lands: PROGRAMMED BY on row 8, JOHN ROWLANDS in two-row letters on rows 10-11, GRAPHICS & MUSIC BY on row 13 and STEVE ROWLANDS on rows 15-16; the rest are spaces, which are solid. PRESS FIRE TO LOAD, the scroller and the copyright are written in later. $7B00, after it, is a spare byte ($BD).
credits_screen from $7900 (row 12, column 16 on the screen): GRAPHICS & MUSIC BY on row 13 and STEVE ROWLANDS on rows 15-16.

credits_screen from $7A00 (row 18, column 32 on the screen) to its end at $7AFF: all spaces, over which PRESS FIRE TO LOAD (row 19), the scroller (rows 21-22) and the copyright (row 24) are written later.

The logo's screen colours, six rows of 40 (240 bytes to $7BF0), which title_2_clear copies to $4000-$40EF: in multicolour bitmap mode each byte gives two of a cell's colours, the high nibble for bit pair 01 and the low for 10.
The logo's colour RAM values, six rows of 40 (240 bytes to $7CE0), copied to $D800-$D8EF: each cell's third colour, for bit pair 11.
The last byte of VIC bank 1, the one the title uses: the VIC shows it in the lines logo_drop_raster opens up above the logo, where it starts no row. title_2_clear zeroes it, so those lines are blank.
The title's entry, where intro_setup jumps once it has patched the title in: JMP title_start.
The NMI handler (title_start and title_2_start point $FFFA/$FFFB here): a single RTI, so RESTORE does nothing. The same byte is the "@" that opens the message after it.
A message in ASCII that nothing prints, to $904B: "------FUZZIES RULE OK!------CLYDE RACLIFFE SAYS "GIVE 'EM SOME SHIT"----".

Changes the background colour ($D021) once a raster line, from a table: A is the number of lines, X and Y the table's address (low, high), written into the code at $906F and $905C/$905D. Between lines it waits in a delay loop, except on every eighth line (Y AND 7 = 0, the 7 kept at $AA); after the last line the background goes back to black. The raster routines use it to colour the credits' and the scroller's letters, which their fonts leave as holes in solid blocks.
Low byte of the operand of the LDA table,Y at $905B: colour_bars writes the table's address here (from X).
High byte of colour_bars' table address (from Y).
Operand of the CPY at $906E: colour_bars' line count (from A).
The raster routines' saved A (with X and Y at irq_save_x and irq_save_y), restored before each RTI.
The raster routines' saved X.
The raster routines' saved Y.
Four 24-byte colour tables for colour_bars, each 16 line colours and 8 zeros. Nothing passes this first one: red, purple, light red, green, cyan, yellow, four whites, and back.
The scroller's 16 line colours (title_raster_3, from line $D8): brown, red, orange, light red, light grey, two yellows, white, light green, cyan, green, two light blues, purple, dark grey and blue.
The 16 line colours of JOHN ROWLANDS, rows 10-11 (title_raster_2 from line $82): brown, dark grey, orange, grey, light grey, two yellows, two whites, and back.
The 16 line colours of STEVE ROWLANDS, rows 15-16 (title_raster_2 from line $AA): blue, dark grey, light blue, light grey, cyan, yellow, four whites, and back.

The first half of the title, THALAMUS PRESENTS. With interrupts off, title_clear sets the screen up; the stack is reset; the IRQ vector at $FFFE/$FFFF goes to logo_raster_top and the NMI's to title_nmi (the RAM vectors, with the KERNAL mapped out by $01 = $35); the CIA interrupts are switched off, the display turned on ($D011 = $1B) and the VIC's raster interrupt set for line 0.

The main loop of the first half. While logo_redraw is set it runs logo_dissolve; otherwise, once logo_wipe_go is set, logo_wipe. The raster routines do the rest, and the last of them leaves the loop for good by jumping to title_2_start.

Raster routine at line 0: sets the background and border (logo_bg, logo_border) and the multicolours $D022/$D023 from logo_mc1/logo_mc2, steps the three fades (bg_fade_in, thalamus_fade_in, bg_fade_out), then places the eight sprites as THALAMUS across the top: pointers from thalamus_frames, colour from the operand at $9165, all at Y = $4A, X from $56 in steps of 24 (29 before the seventh). Sets the next interrupt for line $CA, logo_raster_bottom.
Operand of the LDA #$0F at $9164: THALAMUS's colour, which thalamus_fade_in and thalamus_fade_out write. title_clear starts it at light grey, the background's colour.
Sprite 7's X high bit set ($D010 = $80); all eight sprites at Y = $4A, X from $56 in steps of 24 (29 before the seventh).
Next interrupt at line $CA, logo_raster_bottom; then the registers are restored for the RTI.

Raster routine at line $CA: reuses the eight sprites as PRESENTS at Y = $D2, pointers from presents_frames and colour from the operand at $91E4, X from $5A, then sets the next interrupt for line 0 again.
Operand of the LDA at $91E3: PRESENTS's colour, written by presents_fade_in and presents_fade_out.
Sprite 7's X high bit set; all eight at Y = $D2, X from $5A in steps of 24, 24, 22, 24, 24, 25 and 23.
Next interrupt at line 0, logo_raster_top.

Sets up the first half: memory map $35, black border and background, display off, sprites off, single-colour and unexpanded, and the first half's counters and flags cleared. Arms logo_wipe_go's trigger (the operand at $9413 = 1). Colour RAM to 8 (multicolour characters with colour 0), the screen $4000-$43FF and the character set $4800-$4FFF to 0, the SID's registers to 0. The background fades wait $B0 frames (fade_out_wait). VIC bank 1 with the screen at $4000 and characters at $4800 ($D018 = $02), multicolour characters ($D016 = $D8). Copies the Thalamus logo's layout, logo_layout, to 11 rows of 14 at row 8, column 13 ($414D), and sets both sprite rows' colour to light grey.
Arms the trigger at $9413 (1), then colour RAM to 8, the screen and character set to 0.
Zeroes $D400-$D41C (X from 0 to $1C, past the writable registers to $D418).
The logo's 11 rows of 14 characters, from logo_layout to the screen at $414D, $4175 and on, 40 apart.
Both sprite rows' colour operands, $9165 and $91E4, to light grey.
Sprite pointers for THALAMUS, left to right: T H A L A M U S ($62 $61 $60 $63 $60 $65 $64 $66, sprite_letters).
Sprite pointers for PRESENTS: P R E S E N T S ($6A $69 $67 $66 $67 $68 $62 $66).

Draws the Thalamus logo into the character set a few bits at a time. For 2304 steps Y runs through the 256 bytes nine times over, each step taking 3 bytes ($4800, $48FA and $49F4 plus Y) and ORing in the logo's bits ($5000 and on, logo_chars) under one of the eight masks at dissolve_masks, eight steps with the masks and one without. Over the nine passes every byte gets each mask once, so by the end the set holds the whole logo. A countdown from 15 in dissolve_delay slows each step. Ends by clearing logo_redraw and setting fades_go.
Each step restarts the delay at 15, then ORs one byte of each block under mask X, and moves Y on.
After eight masked bytes, one more step of Y without a mask. The routine ends when Y comes back to 0 here, after 256 groups of nine.
Set by logo_dissolve when it first finishes; until then thalamus_fade_in waits.
The eight bit masks of logo_dissolve and logo_wipe: $22 $90 $44 $21 $50 $24 $42 $28. Between them they hold every bit of a byte.
Steps the background and border through bg_fade_in_colours, one a frame. At the table's end ($FF) it sets logo_redraw and turns all eight sprites on, every frame from then.
Once fades_go is set, steps THALAMUS's colour (the operand at $9165) through sprite_fade_in, one a frame; then hands on to presents_fade_in.
Steps PRESENTS's colour (the operand at $91E4) through the same sprite_fade_in, one a frame, then hands on to thalamus_fade_out.
Waits fade_out_wait ($B0, 176 frames), then steps THALAMUS's colour through thalamus_fade_out_colours, then hands on to presents_fade_out.
Steps PRESENTS's colour (the operand at $91E4) through presents_fade_out_colours, one a frame. At the table's end it sets logo_wipe_go and turns the sprites off.
LDA #$01 as title_clear leaves it: the operand at $9413 is 1 until logo_wipe ends and writes 0, so presents_fade_out, still called every frame, stops setting logo_wipe_go again.
Operand of the LDA at $9412: 1 from title_clear, 0 once logo_wipe has run (see $9412).
Set when PRESENTS has faded: the main loop then runs logo_wipe.

Takes the logo away as logo_dissolve put it there: the same 2304 steps, ANDing where it ORed, so by the end every byte is 0 (no bit is in all eight masks). Then sets bg_fade_out going (bg_fade_go), clears logo_redraw and the trigger at $9413, and blanks the screen ($D011 = $0B).
Each step restarts the delay, then ANDs one byte of each block with mask X.
After eight masked bytes, one more step of Y without a mask; the end, as in logo_dissolve, after 256 groups of nine.
Once bg_fade_go is set, steps the background and border through bg_fade_out_colours, one a frame. At the table's end it jumps, from inside the raster routine, to title_2_start.

The second half, the title screen. title_2_clear sets it up, the stack is reset (dropping the interrupt it came from), the IRQ vector goes to logo_drop_raster and the NMI's to title_nmi; CIA interrupts off, the display blank ($D011 = 0), the raster interrupt at line $2D.
The display blanked, the raster interrupt at line $2D, interrupts on, and title_frame cleared.

The main loop of the second half, once for each frame the raster routines mark in title_frame. When it is 2 (the drop has ended), copies the credits, credits_screen, to the screen from row 6 ($40F0-$43EF). Otherwise it plays a frame of the title tune (music_frame) and reads the joystick in port 2: fire jumps to load_game.
Low byte of the JSR at $94E3: music_frame ($093F), which intro_setup writes again.
High byte of the JSR to music_frame.
Port A of CIA 1 set to inputs ($DC02 = 0), then bit 4 of $DC00, the joystick's fire button in port 2, low when pressed. The JMP at $94F2 is intro_setup's: load_game.
Low byte of the JMP at $94F2: load_game ($2BB5) once intro_setup has patched it; the file holds $1600.
High byte of the fire exit's JMP ($2B for load_game, $16 in the file).

Raster routine at line $2D while the Creatures logo moves: for the number of lines in the operand at $9546, it waits for each line and writes $D011 so that its vertical scroll never matches the line, which keeps the VIC from starting a text row; the bitmap, and the logo at its top, begins that many lines lower. Then it waits for line $FF and takes the next count with logo_drop_step. When the table ends it changes to title_raster_1 at line $31 and sets title_frame to 2.
Operand of the CPX at $9545: the number of lines logo_drop_raster holds the VIC back this frame, from logo_drop_lines (logo_drop_step writes it; title_2_clear starts it at $FF).
Waits for raster line $FF before stepping the drop.
The frame flag the raster routines set (1 a frame, 2 when the logo has landed) and title_2_loop waits on and counts down.
Puts the next of the 196 line counts at logo_drop_lines into the operand at $9546, returning with the carry clear; once all are used it returns with the carry set.

Raster routine at line $31, the top of the title screen: the bitmap at $6000 ($D018 = $08) in bitmap mode ($D011 = $3B), for the Creatures logo, with a border colour for a moment from the operand at $95A4 (always black: border_colours). At line $61 it switches to text with the characters at $7000 ($D018 = $0C). At line $72 it colours PROGRAMMED BY, eight lines from programmed_colours.
Operand of the LDA at $95A3: the border colour title_raster_1 shows for a moment, from border_colours (border_step). Always 0, black.
Waits for line $61, then text mode with the characters at $7000.
Waits for line $72 and colours PROGRAMMED BY, eight lines from programmed_colours, then black.

At line $82, JOHN ROWLANDS's colours (16 lines of gradient_john); at line $9A, GRAPHICS & MUSIC BY's (eight lines of graphics_by_colours), and white after; at line $AA, STEVE ROWLANDS's (16 lines of gradient_steve). Then the next interrupt for line $C9, title_raster_3.
Line $9A: GRAPHICS & MUSIC BY, eight lines of graphics_by_colours, then white.
Line $AA: STEVE ROWLANDS, 16 lines of gradient_steve.
Next interrupt at line $C9, title_raster_3.

Raster routine at line $C9: the background in the colour PRESS FIRE TO LOAD flashes (the operand at $965F). At line $D8 the scroller: characters at $6800 ($D018 = $0A), fine scroll from scroll_fine in $D016, and its 16 lines of colour from gradient_scroller.
Operand of the LDA at $965E: the background colour behind PRESS FIRE TO LOAD, from flash_colours (flash_step). title_2_clear starts it at 1, white.
Waits for line $D8: the scroller's characters ($D018 = $0A) and fine scroll ($D016 = $C0 plus scroll_fine), then its 16 lines of colour.

At line $F1, back to the characters at $7000 and no fine scroll, the copyright line's nine colours from copyright_colours, a border colour for a moment (the operand at $96BD, black), then a black border and background.
Operand of the LDA at $96BC: title_raster_3's moment of border colour, from border_colours like $95A4.

Steps the frame's effects (border_step, copyright_step, press_fire_step, fade_step_unused), sets multicolour bitmap mode for the top again ($D016 = $D8, $D011 = $3B), marks the frame in title_frame and sets the next interrupt for line $31, title_raster_1.

After copyright_wait ($40 frames), writes the copyright line onto row 24 from the middle out, one character each way a frame, from copyright_text: indexes 20 down to 1 (copyright_left) and 20 up to 39 (copyright_right).

After press_fire_wait ($60 frames), writes PRESS FIRE TO LOAD onto row 19 the same way, from press_fire_text. Once it is all there, each frame steps its flash (flash_step) and the scroller (scroll_step).
Every seven frames counts fade_count from 0 to 15 and builds 16 plus the count in A, then three NOPs, where a store of A would fit; nothing uses the value. What it once wrote is not known.
The scroller's fine scroll, 0-7, which title_raster_3 puts in $D016.
fade_step_unused's frame counter.
fade_step_unused's count, 0 to 15.
Frames before PRESS FIRE TO LOAD starts to appear ($60 from title_2_clear).
The next character of PRESS FIRE TO LOAD to write leftwards (20 down to 1), and the count of those still to write.
The next character of PRESS FIRE TO LOAD to write rightwards (20 up to 39).
Puts the next colour of flash_colours in the operand at $965F (the background behind PRESS FIRE TO LOAD), going back to the start at the $FF.
PRESS FIRE TO LOAD's colours, one a frame: 8 white, 4 light grey, 4 grey, 4 dark grey, 24 black, then dark grey, grey and light grey back up, 56 frames in all.
The next entry of flash_colours.
Every second frame puts the next of border_colours in the two border operands ($95A4 and $96BD), back to the start at the $FF. The table is all black, so nothing changes.

The scroller, rows 21 and 22 at three pixels a frame: takes 3 from scroll_fine and, when it passes 0, moves both rows ($4348-$436F, $4370-$4397) one character left and writes the new column at the right. Each letter is two characters wide and two high: its left column is the letter's code (top) and code + $80 (bottom), its right column code + $40 and code + $C0.
scroll_half set: writes the right column of the letter in scroll_letter and moves the text pointer on (the 16-bit operand at $9841).

Reads the next character of the text (the operand at $9841/$9842 points into scroll_text): 0 starts the text again, $FF pauses the scroller for $50 frames (scroll_pause); anything else, ANDed with $3F, is a letter, whose left column is written here.
Low byte of the LDA at $9840: the scroller's place in scroll_text. title_2_clear sets it to $9A79, the text's start, and scroll_step moves it on.
High byte of the scroller's place in scroll_text.
1 when the right column of the letter in scroll_letter is still to be written.
The letter (its code ANDed with $3F) being written into the scroller.
Frames the scroller is held still after a $FF in the text.

Sets up the second half: display off, black border and background, sprite expansion and priority cleared, the idle bytes $7FFF and $3FFF zeroed, the drop, flash, fade and scroller counters cleared, the flash colour white, the copyright and PRESS FIRE counters at 20 with their waits ($40, $60), and the first line count $FF. Clears colour RAM and the screen, then copies the logo's colours to its top six rows (logo_screen to $4000-$40EF, logo_colour to $D800-$D8EF).
Colour RAM and the screen $4000-$43FF to 0.
The logo's colours: logo_screen to $4000-$40EF, logo_colour to $D800-$D8EF.

VIC bank 1, the screen at $4000 and the bitmap at $6000 ($D018 = $08). The STA at $9906 writes $D8 to $0016 in zero page; $D8 is the value the raster routines give $D016, so this looks like a slip for $D016, and it does no harm since they set $D016 every frame. Then $D022/$D023 cyan and light blue, and the title tune starts (music_play, with the tune at $3800 as intro_setup patched it).
Operand of the LDX at $9913: the high byte of the tune's header for music_play, $38 from intro_setup (the file holds $00).
Operand of the LDY at $9915: the header's low byte, $00 from intro_setup (the file holds $9E).
Low byte of the JSR at $9917: music_play ($08D0), which intro_setup writes again.
High byte of the JSR to music_play.
LDA #$00 then three NOPs where a store would fit, as in fade_step_unused; then the scroller's text pointer is set to the start of scroll_text, $9A79.
The copyright line in screen codes, 40 characters: "(C) MCMXC THALAMUS SOFTWARE", with a stray $83 after it at $9952.
PRESS FIRE TO LOAD in screen codes, 40 characters, then 16 more spaces to $998A that nothing reads.
The copyright line's nine line colours: blue, light blue, cyan, white, yellow, light red, red, orange, black. Two zeros follow, unused.
GRAPHICS & MUSIC BY's eight line colours: light grey, white, white, light green, light grey, grey, dark grey, dark grey. The last two bytes, $999E-$999F, are dark grey too and unused.
PROGRAMMED BY's eight line colours: light blue, white, white, light green, cyan, light blue, blue, blue; two more blues after them, unused.
The next entry of border_colours.
border_step's two-frame counter.
The next of the logo_drop_lines (to 196).
Frames before the copyright line starts to appear ($40 from title_2_clear).
The next character of the copyright line to write leftwards, and the count still to write.
The next character of the copyright line to write rightwards.

196 line counts, one a frame, for logo_drop_raster: the number of lines the Creatures logo is pushed down. They go from 255 down to 1, up to 249 and down to 1 again, in big steps near 255 and small ones near 1: the logo rises from the bottom of the screen to the top, drops back nearly to the bottom and rises again, slowing as it nears the top. Four more 1s and a 0 follow, unused, to $9A78.

The scroller's text in ASCII (upper case; scroll_step keeps the low six bits): "CLYDE RADCLIFFE EXTERMINATES ALL THE UNFRIENDLY REPULSIVE EARTH-RIDDEN SLIME - CREATURES -", a $FF pause, "AN APEX COMPUTER PRODUCTION ADDITIONAL WORK BY ANDY SMITH, MILES BARRY AND ANDY ROBERTS", and the 0 that starts it again at $9B59.
scroll_text's last 24 spaces before its end at $9B59. The label is where the scroller's pointer (the operand at $9841) stood when the snapshot was taken.
After the text's end: the tail of an older text ("LK -", spaces and a 0), never read.
The background and border after the logo is wiped: 18 frames of light grey, 4 of grey, 4 of dark grey, 32 of black, then $FF, the end.
Set by logo_wipe: bg_fade_out runs while it is set.
Frames thalamus_fade_out waits before it starts ($B0 from title_clear).
The next entry of sprite_fade_in for PRESENTS.
The next entry of thalamus_fade_out_colours.
The next entry of presents_fade_out_colours.
The next entry of bg_fade_out_colours.
border_step's border colours: 17 of black, then $FF.

PRESENTS's colours after THALAMUS has faded: 25 frames of dark grey, then on through thalamus_fade_out_colours, which has no $FF before it, to that table's end. So PRESENTS holds for half a second and fades the same way.
THALAMUS's colours as it fades out: dark grey, 5 of black, 5 of dark grey, 5 of grey, 20 of light grey (the background), then $FF at $9C17.
The colours THALAMUS and then PRESENTS fade in through: 25 frames of light grey (the background), 5 of grey, 5 of dark grey, 5 of black, then dark grey, and $FF.
Set every frame by bg_fade_in once the background is up: the main loop runs logo_dissolve while it is set.
The next entry of sprite_fade_in for THALAMUS.
The next entry of bg_fade_in_colours.
The first half's background and border: 32 frames of black, 4 of dark grey, 4 of grey, 21 of light grey, then $FF.
The countdown from 15 that slows each step of logo_dissolve and logo_wipe.
The first half's background colour ($D021), from the fades.
The first half's border colour ($D020), from the fades.
The logo's first shared multicolour, $D022: dark grey.
The logo's second shared multicolour, $D023: grey.
The Thalamus logo's characters, 11 rows of 14 (codes 0-$4C of logo_chars; 0 is blank), which title_clear copies to the screen at row 8, column 13.
logo_layout's row 1, screen row 9.
logo_layout's row 2, screen row 10.
logo_layout's row 3, screen row 11.
logo_layout's row 4, screen row 12.
logo_layout's row 5, screen row 13.
logo_layout's row 6, screen row 14.
logo_layout's row 7, screen row 15.
logo_layout's row 8, screen row 16.
logo_layout's row 9, screen row 17.
logo_layout's row 10, screen row 18, the last; logo_layout ends at $9D21.
